building.name: Wisconsin Commercial Building Code (Wis. Admin. Code chs. SPS 361 to 366), adopted by reference in Madison General Ordinances Sec. 29.22
building.edition: 2021 International Building Code with Wisconsin changes (DSPS inserts headed 'September 1, 2025 Wisconsin Commercial Building Code, SPS 361 - SPS 366')
building.local_amendments_note: Sec. 29.23, 'Items to be enforced over Wisconsin Administrative Code', adds city items: partition construction around dwelling units and lodging rooms, fire escapes, windows and courts, fire protection within buildings, exits, swimming pools, exit doors, sanitation (dwelling units and rooming houses), isolation of fire hazards and building near waste disposal sites. Sec. 29.34 sets the Capitol Fire District. No item concerns toilet partitions or the number of toilets in commercial buildings. State law limits city ordinances to ones that conform to the statewide code (state pack: DSPS Act 270 FAQ).
building.effective_note: The date is the heading of the DSPS code inserts; no DSPS page stating the effective date could be opened (the DSPS news release of July 30, 2025 and the fall 2025 newsletter returned 404). A search summary of those DSPS documents says plans submitted on or after November 1, 2025 must meet the updated code; not read. DSPS: 'The code in effect on the date a valid plan submittal is received' governs review.
building.quote: 29.22 - ADOPTION BY REFERENCE. The Wis. Admin. Code Chapters: SPS 320 (Uniform Dwelling Code — Administration and Enforcement); SPS 321 [...]; SPS 322 [...]; SPS 328 [...]; SPS 361 (Commercial Building Code – Administration And Enforcement); SPS 362 (Commercial Building Code – Buildings And Structures); SPS 363 (Commercial Building Code – Energy Conservation); SPS 366 (Existing Buildings) SPS 375-379 (Buildings Constructed Prior to 1914). fixtures.basis: Madison adopts SPS 362, which carries Wisconsin's toilet-count rules, by reference (Sec. 29.22). The only city text on toilets, Sec. 29.23(9)(a), covers dwelling units and rooming houses ('at least one (1) water closet for every seven (7) roomers'), not offices, restaurants or schools. Chapter 18 (plumbing) holds no count. State law requires city building ordinances to conform to the statewide code (state pack). The state pack's worked examples stand.
fixtures.quote: (9) Sanitation. (Ref. Wis. Admin. Code ch. SPS 362). (a) Toilet Rooms and Washing Facilities. Every dwelling unit shall contain a kitchen sink, a flush water closet, a lavatory basin, and a bathtub or shower all in good working condition [...] All other buildings shall have at least one (1) water closet for every seven (7) roomers or fraction thereof.
fixtures.second_note: Madison's appeals board hears variances from the state rule itself, e.g. Legistar file 30894 (2013), 'appealing IBC 2902.2', and file 52422 (2018), 'appealing IBC 2902.3.1': the city applies the state table.

permit.exempt_list_quote: 29.07 - APPLICATION FOR PERMIT, PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS. (1) No person shall erect or construct any building or structure whatever, or add to, enlarge, move, improve, alter, convert, extend or demolish any building or structure, or cause the same to be done, or commence any work covered by this code on any structure without first obtaining a building permit therefor from the Director of the Building Inspection Division; provided, however, that the Director of the Building Inspection Division may authorize minor improvements not involving structural alterations, change in use and which do not exceed a cost of five hundred dollars ($500) without requiring a building permit to be issued. Such permit shall be issued in the name of the owner.
permit.note: Madison's ordinance has no list of exempt work. It requires a permit to 'improve' or 'alter' any building and lets the Director waive it for minor improvements of $500 or less with no structural alteration or change in use. Toilet partitions are not named. The city's permit chart says wall-mounted cabinets need no permit and its non-residential repairs page sends 'general repairs over $500' to Building Inspection, 608-266-4551 ext. 2 (both read through WebFetch, which summarises). The state's plan review rule (as DSPS summarises SPS 361.30) excepts 'repairs, replacements, or minor alterations that the building official agrees don't need plan approval'; the rule text itself could not be opened.
permit.second_quote: Summary of the page as read through WebFetch (not verbatim): building permits are needed for doors, roofing, siding and windows; for general repairs over $500, contact Building Inspection at 608-266-4551 ext. 2.
permit.third_quote: If you are only adding or replacing wall-mounted cabinets, you do not need a permit.
permit.office: City of Madison Building Inspection Division

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Madison job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Wisconsin rules Madison enforces.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Madison state office buildings, university halls, hospitals and schools, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law and Wisconsin's building rules set the sizes. In Madison, the city's Building Inspection Division reviews commercial building plans of every size in place of the state.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Wisconsin's building rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. Madison adopts them as the state writes them and adds no count of its own for offices, restaurants or schools. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** the City of Madison's Building Inspection Division issues building permits. Madison's building rules require a permit to alter or improve any building. The division's director may allow minor improvements without one when they cost $500 or less and involve no structural change and no change of use. The rules list no exempt work and don't name toilet partitions. Ask Building Inspection (608-266-4551) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Madison Building Inspection Division
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building. A restaurant that needs six or more toilets in total, as at 400 people, must also have a family or assisted-use toilet room, which counts toward the total. Wisconsin's rules don't say how an odd number splits between stalls and urinals, so confirm that with Madison's building plan reviewers (608-266-4551).
page.install_rule: Building permits in Madison come from the city's Building Inspection Division. Madison's code sets no city general contractor license, and permit applicants list their subcontractors. Wisconsin does not license contractors for commercial work at the state level. Confirm with the Building Inspection Division and the Wisconsin Department of Safety and Professional Services. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Madison's code sets no city general contractor license, and Wisconsin does not license contractors for commercial work at the state level.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Wisconsin repealed its own wage law for public jobs in 2017, so set wage rates apply only on federally funded work. For a carpenter on building work in Dane County that rate is $42.45 an hour plus $28.78 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 5.5% in Madison: 5% state and 0.5% Dane County. Madison has no city sales tax.
page.buyers_extra: - **State offices and university buildings:** one material and one hardware standard across many buildings, with heavy-duty hardware for restrooms that fill between classes and sessions.

SPS 361 to 366: the 2021 International Building Code with Wisconsin changes, DSPS inserts dated September 1, 2025), adopted by reference in Section 29.22 of the Madison General Ordinances (Chapter 29, Building Code) and enforced by the City of Madison Building Inspection Division; Wisconsin Plumbing Code (chs. notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether replacing or adding anchored toilet partitions in an existing commercial restroom needs a City of Madison building permit, and whether the $500 waiver is still the rule (Building Inspection, 608-266-4551, ext. 2 for plan review).

Chapters 29 and 18 of the Madison General Ordinances were read as enacted in March 2021 (Legistar files 63535 and 63536), because Municode blocks automated access; Legistar shows later changes only to fees (29.09), the appeals board (29.21) and the adoption list (29.22, adding SPS 327). Check Sections 29.07 and 29.22 on Municode in a browser.
cityofmadison.com and revenue.wi.gov pages were read through WebFetch, which summarises: check the quoted lines in a browser. The ordinance PDFs, the DSPS PDFs and sam.gov were read directly.

The date the 2021-based Wisconsin code took effect is taken from the heading of the DSPS inserts (September 1, 2025); a search summary of DSPS documents that returned 404 says plans submitted from November 1, 2025 must meet it. Confirm with DSPS, 608-266-2112.

No Madison ordinance on single-user restroom signs or all-gender rooms was found; the city's Engineering page describes gender-inclusive restrooms in the city's own buildings only. Chapter 39 of the ordinances (equal opportunities) was not read.

Madison's code keeps city items it enforces on top of the state code (Section 29.23: fire protection, exits, housing sanitation and others); none concerns toilet partitions or toilet counts in commercial buildings.
No change to the 5.5% sales tax is listed on the Department of Revenue's rate page; the Department's address lookup was not used.
A city living wage or other wage rule on City of Madison contracts was not researched.
The buyers bullet on state offices and university buildings and the four building types in the lead are editorial, not sourced.
